To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) lemmatization is better than stemming, (2) lemmatized words are better index terms than unlemmatized words, (3) syntactic dependencies are better index terms that unlemmatized or lemmatized single words, (4) the best results are obtained by combining lemmatization, syntactic parsing, and the use of syntactic dependencies as index terms.
lemmatization is a better alternative than stemming for text retrieval and that the use of shallow parsing for text retrieval is not a good idea.

1) lemmatization, stemming, and syntactic parsing are effective techniques to improve the quality of the index terms; 2) lemmatized index terms perform slightly better than stemmed index terms, but they are not significantly different from them; and 3) syntactically parsed index terms perform much better than lemmatized or stemmed index terms.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following questions: How to improve Text Retrieval by using linguistic information at both word and phrase levels? What is the best way to use the syntactic dependency information detected by the parser in Text Retrieval? What are the differences between the results obtained by using lemmatization, stemming and shallow parsing in a Text Retrieval application?

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, in the particular case of the corpus used for this article, lemmatization is more effective than stemming for word-level indexing and that syntactic indexing, though less effective, has the advantage of being able to capture linguistic variation at phrase level.
the use of shallow parsing in text retrieval is a promising research line, but it is still too early to make definitive statements on the advantages and disadvantages of the approach.
, in spite of the fact that syntactic parsing can improve the retrieval results, the improvement is not so significant to justify the extra processing time and resources required for parsing.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the application of shallow parsing for indexing is an effective alternative to stemming.
we are trying to find a way to use the syntactic dependencies of a word in a sentence as index terms for text retrieval.
we have shown that the application of a shallow parser to Text Retrieval can provide a better alternative to stemming, and that it is also possible to use the parser for the selection of index terms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
syntactic parsing and shallow parsing can be applied successfully to Text Retrieval.
shallow parsing can be used as an effective tool in the context of Text Retrieval, and can be applied to any language for which a shallow parser is available.
shallow parsing can be used to obtain better retrieval results, even when the parser is trained on a different language.
